verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. Despite much research, we still know very little about this conjecture. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract surveys the log-rank conjecture relating communication complexity to matrix rank, but says nothing about representation theory, CNF formulas, or minimal orders of linear representations of permutation actions—the specific bridge claimed by the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Applications of Monotone Rank to Complexity Theory
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Raz's recent result \cite{Raz2010} has rekindled people's interest in the study of \emph{tensor rank}, the generalization of matrix rank to high dimensions, by showing its connections to arithmetic formulas. In this paper, we follow Raz's work and show that \emph{monotone rank}, the monotone variant of tensor rank and matrix rank, has applications in algebraic complexity, quantum computing and communication complexity. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses monotone/tensor rank applications to communication complexity (generalizing the log-rank conjecture to multiparty settings), but says nothing about linear representations of permutation actions of CNF formulas or character-theoretic minimal orders. It shares the 'rank in communication complexity' vocabulary but does not address the specific conjecture.
